frisbii-core.summary: Foundation for every skill in the pack: checks the connection and MCP access, detects Pay vs Billing, paces calls for the rate limit, keeps everything read-only and formats money and dates consistently.
frisbii-core.audience: Frisbii Billing and Frisbii Pay merchants (installed alongside every other skill in the pack); Frisbii CS and product marketing
what: The shared rulebook the other 18 skills rely on. Before any data call it confirms which Frisbii account is connected (`get_account`) and whether MCP access is on the merchant's plan (`get_token_allowance`). If access is blocked it stops with a clear message instead of failing tool calls.

It works out whether the account runs subscriptions (Billing) or payments only (Pay), keeps calls within the server's limit of about 3 per minute by preferring the snapshot `count_*` and revenue tools over paging lists, and enforces the pack's read-only rule: no tool that creates, changes, refunds, retries or cancels anything is ever called.

It also fixes the conventions every report must follow: minor vs major money units, never adding across currencies or VAT treatments, quoting the snapshot `as_of` time, which subscription end date means churn, and the recovery next steps to show whenever failed or overdue payments appear.
triggers: Any Frisbii Billing or Pay data question answered with the Frisbii Billing & Pay MCP server, with or without another skill.
Loaded first by every other skill in the pack.
examples: "How many active subscriptions do we have?"
A pre-flight check, then a single snapshot count with its as-of time
"Why isn't the Frisbii connector returning anything?"
A check of account and MCP entitlement, with a plain explanation (e.g. MCP not on the plan) and who can fix it
"Cancel this subscription for me."
A polite refusal: the pack is read-only, with a pointer to the Frisbii dashboard

files.references/recovery-next-steps.md: Wording for the next-steps block shown when failed or overdue invoices appear, and the rules for drafting customer messages

notes: Pay vs Billing detection is a heuristic (live subscriptions vs settled transactions in the last 90 days).
The ~3 calls/minute rate limit is the main constraint on report size; each skill states its call budget.
Not yet validated against live data: the MCP entitlement is still being enabled on the test accounts.

month-end-close.summary: Month-end close report for Billing merchants: MRR as of the snapshot, new vs churned subscriptions and their MRR, invoices raised split into paid, open and failed, and refunds paid out.
month-end-close.audience: Frisbii Billing merchants (finance and founders); Frisbii CS
month-end-close.week: Week 1 (26 Oct 2026), launch episode; refresher in week 6
what: Turns month-end into one prompt. In about eight snapshot calls the agent reports current recurring revenue by plan, committed vs already-cancelling MRR, new and ended subscriptions with the MRR each added or removed, invoices raised in the month by outcome, and refunds paid out.

It is careful about what the numbers mean: MRR is the current book as of the snapshot time (not reconstructed for the last day of the month), churn uses the date a subscription actually ended, and amounts are never added across currencies.
Pay-only accounts without subscriptions get a short payments view instead; payout-reconciliation is the Pay equivalent.
triggers: Closing the month, a month-end summary or an MRR snapshot.
"How did October go?" or new vs churned subscriptions for a month.
examples: "Close October for me."
A month-end report: MRR by plan, new vs ended subscriptions and MRR, invoices paid/open/failed, refunds
"What's our MRR right now?"
Current MRR by plan with committed vs scheduled-to-cancel split and the as-of time
"How many subscriptions did we lose last month?"
Ended subscriptions and the MRR they removed, using the actual end date
notes: Opening MRR can't be reconstructed (upgrades and downgrades aren't visible), so net movement is new minus ended only.
Not yet validated against live data.

customer-360.summary: One-page briefing on a single customer before a call: profile, subscriptions, recurring revenue, invoices, balance or credit, payment methods with card expiry, and dunning status.
customer-360.audience: Frisbii Pay and Billing merchants (account managers, support, finance); Frisbii CS and sales
what: Finds the customer from a handle, email, company or person name (asking when several match), then builds the briefing mostly from one call, `get_customer_billing_overview`, which returns profile, all subscriptions, open and recent invoices and stored payment methods.

It adds recurring revenue, outstanding balance or credit and dunning status only when relevant, flags cards that expire before the next renewal, and ends with next steps when invoices are overdue, including an offer to draft a card-update message for the merchant to send.
triggers: "Tell me about customer X", "brief me before my call with X".
A pasted customer handle, email or company name.
examples: "Brief me on anna@example.com before my call."
A one-page summary: status, MRR, open invoices, payment method and anything needing attention
"What's going on with Acme A/S?"
A list of matching customers if ambiguous, then the briefing for the chosen one
"Why did cust-0042's last payment fail?"
The failed invoice with the decline reason and the likely fix
notes: Card fingerprints and cross-customer card matching are deliberately excluded.
Not yet validated against live data.

card-expiry-sweep.summary: Finds stored cards that expire before the next charge or renewal so the merchant can get them updated before payments fail.
card-expiry-sweep.audience: Frisbii Pay merchants with cards on file (also Billing); Frisbii CS
card-expiry-sweep.week: Week 3 (9 Nov 2026), Black Friday prep; refresher in week 8
what: Pages through stored payment methods (there is no expiry filter on the MCP), buckets active cards into already expired, expiring this month and expiring before the chosen horizon, and optionally checks the top cases against the customer's next renewal date.

The output is a list for the merchant's team (customer handle and masked card only). If asked, the agent drafts a short card-update message for the merchant to send through their own channel; it never sends anything.
triggers: Expiring cards, cards expiring before Black Friday or a renewal.
"Which customers need a new card?" or preventing failed payments.
examples: "Which cards expire before Black Friday?"
Counts per bucket and a table of cards expiring by 27 Nov, soonest first
"Any cards expiring before their renewal this month?"
Flagged cards with the renewal date they will miss
"Draft a message asking them to update their card."
A short, polite draft for the merchant to send
notes: Capped at 10 pages (~1,000 payment methods) per run because of the rate limit; partial coverage is always disclosed.
The card `exp_date` format must be confirmed on live data.
Not yet validated against live data.

account-hygiene.summary: Housekeeping check: stuck subscriptions, draft and long-unpaid invoices, customers holding credit, stale coupons and customers without a live subscription.
account-hygiene.audience: Frisbii Billing and Pay merchants (operations, finance); Frisbii CS
what: Runs seven snapshot checks and presents them as a health table with what each finding usually means: pending and on-hold subscriptions, unfinalised invoices, pending invoices due over 30 days ago, failed or dunning invoices, customers holding credit, coupons that are expired or exhausted but still active, and how many customers have no active subscription.
It suggests a clean-up list for the merchant to work through in the Frisbii dashboard and never cancels, voids or deletes anything itself.
triggers: An account health check, tidying up, stale or stuck subscriptions.
Leftover test data, or preparing the account before a busy period.
examples: "Give my account a health check."
A table of seven checks with counts, amounts and a suggested clean-up list
"Do we have subscriptions stuck in pending?"
Pending and on-hold counts with what they usually indicate
"Is there leftover test data?"
The newest customers with their test flag, on request
notes: "Subscription with no payment method" can't be filtered on the MCP, so it isn't part of the check.
Not yet validated against live data.

promo-readiness.summary: Pre-campaign check of coupons, discounts and plans before a promotion such as Black Friday.
promo-readiness.audience: Frisbii Billing merchants (marketing, ecommerce, finance); Frisbii CS
what: Reads active coupons, the discounts they reference and the plans they apply to, then checks each coupon against the campaign dates: validity window, remaining redemptions, broken or inactive discount links, currency mismatches, superseded plans, duplicate codes and suspiciously large discounts.
Results come back as ready / warning / blocker per coupon with exactly what to fix in the Frisbii dashboard. The skill changes nothing.
triggers: "Is my Black Friday promo set up right?"
Checking coupons or discount codes, or a campaign readiness check.
examples: "Is my Black Friday promo ready?"
A coupon-by-coupon status table with blockers to fix before launch
"Check coupon CYBER26."
Validity, redemptions, linked discount and eligible plans for that code
"Will our coupons last the whole weekend?"
Coupons expiring or running out of redemptions before Cyber Monday
notes: Falls back to `get_plan` if `list_plans` returns empty (known issue, still to be confirmed on live data).
Not yet validated against live data.

payment-method-mix.summary: How customers pay: method mix by volume, success rate per method, outstanding failures per method and customer geography.
payment-method-mix.audience: Frisbii Pay merchants (ecommerce, payments, finance); Frisbii CS and sales
what: Shows settled volume and share per payment method (card, MobilePay Subscriptions, wallets, bank transfer and others) for the period and against the previous period, the all-time success vs failure rate per method, outstanding unsettled transactions for the top methods, and where customers are based.
Each figure is labelled with its time basis, because the transaction count filters on settlement date and failed payments never settle.
triggers: Payment methods, card vs MobilePay, which methods fail most.
Whether to add or promote a payment method before a peak.
examples: "Card vs MobilePay: how do my customers pay?"
Method mix by count and volume with the trend vs the previous period
"Which payment method fails most?"
Success rate per method (all time) and outstanding failures for the period
"Where are my customers based?"
Top 10 countries by customer count next to the method mix
notes: Transactions can't be grouped by country, so a per-market method split isn't available.
Success rates are all-time; the period mix is settled payments only.
Not yet validated against live data.

peak-pulse.summary: Near-live pulse of payments and sign-ups during a peak such as Black Friday, in three calls per refresh.
peak-pulse.audience: Frisbii Pay merchants during peaks (ecommerce, operations); also Billing for sign-ups
what: Each refresh reports settled volume by payment method, today's payment outcomes (settled vs failed vs in progress, giving a success rate) and new subscriptions, plus what changed since the last refresh. The first run adds a comparison with the same weekday a week earlier.
It is labelled near-live: the snapshot behind the counts usually lags by a few minutes, so the as-of time is shown prominently and refreshes are limited to one every five minutes.
triggers: "How is Black Friday going?", "how are payments doing today?".
Asking for a live view or to refresh the peak numbers.
examples: "How are payments doing today?"
Settled volume by method, success rate and new sign-ups, compared with last week
"Refresh."
The same three figures with the change since the last refresh
"Is our success rate normal?"
Today's rate vs the same weekday last week, with a flag if it is 5+ points lower
notes: Snapshot lag on a busy account must be measured before Black Friday.
Consider a temporary rate-limit increase for BFCM week.
Not yet validated against live data.

failed-payment-triage.summary: Diagnoses failed and overdue payments: how much, why (soft vs hard declines), what is likely recoverable, where it is concentrated and what to do next.
failed-payment-triage.audience: Frisbii Pay and Billing merchants (finance, operations); Frisbii CS
failed-payment-triage.week: Week 6 (30 Nov 2026), Cyber Monday; refresher in week 12
what: Combines invoice counts by state, everything currently in dunning, the most recent failed payments with their decline detail and the largest overdue exposures. Failures are bucketed into soft declines, hard declines, processing errors and methods without codes, with the top reasons by amount.

It ends with specific next steps: hard declines need a new payment method (with an offer to draft a card-update message for the merchant to send), soft declines usually recover through dunning, and failed invoices outside any dunning flow need a dunning plan. It never retries payments.
triggers: Failed payments, declined cards, overdue invoices.
Money stuck after Black Friday or Cyber Monday, or "how much can I recover?".
examples: "Why are payments failing?"
Failures by bucket and top reasons, with what is likely recoverable
"How much can I recover since Black Friday?"
The recoverable amount (soft declines plus processing errors) and the largest exposures
"Retry them all."
A refusal to retry (read-only) with a pointer to the dashboard
notes: Reason classification uses up to 100 recent failures (about a one-month window); the full set is available as an export.
The `error_state` field names must be confirmed on live data.
Not yet validated against live data.

promo-cohort-quality.summary: Compares subscribers acquired with a discount against full-price subscribers from the same window: still active, leaving and already ended.
what: Defines the cohort as subscriptions created in the promo window, splits it into discounted (from discount applications) and full-price, and compares how many are still active, have a cancellation scheduled or have already ended. It adds the cohort's recurring revenue and coupon redemption counts, and optionally a non-promo baseline cohort.
It is explicit that a December read is early: most cancellations appear after the first renewal, so it suggests re-running in February.
triggers: "Were my Black Friday customers worth the discount?"
Whether promo sign-ups stuck, or discounted vs full-price retention.
examples: "Were my Black Friday customers worth the discount?"
Discounted vs full-price retention so far, cohort MRR and coupon redemptions
"How is coupon BF2026 doing?"
The cohort for that discount: joined, still active, leaving, ended
"Compare with a normal month."
A baseline cohort from four weeks earlier
notes: Discount counts are applications, not subscriptions; the split is approximate when several promo discounts apply.
MRR can't be split by discount from the snapshot; an export is offered.
Not yet validated against live data.

dispute-monitor.summary: Chargeback and dispute overview: disputes by reason, state and outcome, ones waiting for a response, dispute rate and change vs the previous period.
dispute-monitor.audience: Frisbii Pay merchants (finance, risk, customer service)
what: Uses the dispute snapshot to show disputes raised in the period by reason, by state and outcome (won, lost, withdrawn), everything waiting for the merchant's response, the dispute rate against settled payments and the change vs the previous period.

Next steps are tailored to the dominant reason, e.g. responding before the deadline, reviewing cancellation flows or risk rules, and a flag when the dispute rate approaches card-scheme monitoring levels.
triggers: Chargebacks or disputes, especially after Black Friday.
Dispute rate, or which disputes need a response.
examples: "How many chargebacks since Black Friday?"
Disputes by reason with amounts, rate and change vs the previous period
"Which disputes need a response?"
Count and amount waiting for a response, with the next step
"What's our win rate on disputes?"
Won vs resolved disputes for the period
notes: The MCP exposes counts and amounts only, not individual disputes; acting on a dispute happens in the dashboard.
Not yet validated against live data.

renewal-radar.summary: Annual and high-value renewals in the next 30–60 days, with value and scheduled cancellations flagged.
renewal-radar.audience: Frisbii Billing merchants (account managers, finance); Frisbii CS
what: Ranks plans by MRR, identifies annual (and other long-interval) plans from their billing interval, pages subscriptions on those plans and keeps the ones renewing inside the horizon. Each renewal shows customer, plan, quantity and list value, with renewals that already carry a scheduled cancellation flagged.
It suggests preparing for the largest renewals and those at risk, with customer-360 and card-expiry-sweep as follow-ups.
triggers: Upcoming renewals, "which annual contracts renew in January?".
Renewals at risk, or preparing account managers before the new year.
examples: "Which annual renewals are coming up?"
Renewals in the next 60 days, soonest first, with value
"January renewals at risk?"
Renewals with a cancellation already scheduled and the revenue involved
"Renewals over DKK 10,000 in Q1."
High-value renewals filtered by list value
notes: There is no renewal-date filter, so it pages up to 5 annual plans × 2 pages; caps are disclosed.
Plan interval field names must be confirmed on live data.
Not yet validated against live data.

year-in-review.summary: Shareable annual recap: payment volume and method mix, recurring revenue growth, new customers and subscribers, top plans and best month, with an optional LinkedIn post.
year-in-review.audience: Frisbii Pay and Billing merchants (founders, marketing); Frisbii marketing
what: Picks Pay and Billing sections automatically and builds headlines from snapshot data: volume processed and year-on-year growth, payments by method, best month, MRR now and from subscriptions started this year, new customers and subscriptions, and top plans.
On request it drafts a short LinkedIn-ready post, using percentages instead of revenue if the merchant prefers and never including customer data.
triggers: A year in review, annual recap or wrap-up.
"How was 2026?" or something to share about the year.
examples: "My 2026 in review."
Headlines, payments by method, top plans and a month-by-month view
"Make me a LinkedIn post about our year."
A 4–6 line post with growth percentages and milestones
"How did this year compare with last year?"
Year-on-year growth in volume and customers
notes: The month-by-month view depends on `count_transactions` accepting `group_by=settled_month`; it is skipped if not.
Not yet validated against live data.

board-pack.summary: Quarter- or year-end board summary: MRR movement, committed vs at-risk revenue, churn estimate, cohorts, plan mix, collections and add-on revenue, as slides or a one-pager.
board-pack.audience: Frisbii Billing merchants (founders, CFOs, finance); Frisbii CS for QBRs
what: Runs about twelve snapshot calls for the period: MRR and plan mix, committed vs already-cancelling revenue, live, new and ended subscriptions with their MRR, monthly cohorts, invoiced vs collected vs failed, add-on revenue net of VAT and credits, and paying customers.

Derived figures (net new MRR, estimated churn rate, at-risk share, collection rate) are labelled as estimates, and nothing is presented as a forecast. Output is a slide-by-slide pack (using a branded slides skill when available) or a one-pager.
triggers: A board pack, board or investor update, QBR numbers.
A quarterly or year-end summary, or "the board slide".
examples: "Board pack for Q4."
Six slides: headline, MRR movement, subscriptions and cohorts, plan mix, collections, definitions
"Year-end investor update as a one-pager."
A compact report with the same metrics
"What was our churn rate last quarter?"
An estimated churn rate with how it was derived
notes: Churn rate and period-start counts are estimates because the snapshot is current-state only.
Not yet validated against live data.

payout-reconciliation.summary: Reconciles payouts for a period against captures, refunds and fees so each payout can be matched to the bank statement.
payout-reconciliation.audience: Frisbii Pay merchants (finance, accountants); also Billing
payout-reconciliation.week: Weeks 1 and 11 (26 Oct 2026 and 4 Jan 2027), Pay alternative
what: Lists payouts paid in the period with bank reference, then breaks each one down (up to ten) into gross captures, refunds, fees by type and net, checking that net matches the payout amount. Failed and still-processing payouts are flagged.
It handles the unit difference between tools (payouts in minor units, settlement reports in major units) and explains timing differences between sales and payouts rather than treating them as errors.
triggers: Reconciling payouts or matching bank deposits.
"What did Frisbii pay me in October?", fees for the month, payout vs sales differences.
examples: "Reconcile my October payouts."
Each payout with bank reference, gross, refunds, fees and net, all checked
"What fees did I pay last month?"
Fees by type and as a share of gross
"Why are payouts lower than sales?"
An explanation of fees, refunds and timing using the period's captures
notes: Settlement breakdowns are fetched for at most 10 payouts per run; the rest show net amounts only.
Not yet validated against live data.

churn-and-retention.summary: Churn trend over three months, churn by plan, voluntary vs involuntary split where available, revenue scheduled to cancel and at-risk segments.
churn-and-retention.audience: Frisbii Billing merchants (founders, growth, customer success)
what: Counts subscriptions and MRR that ended each month over the last three months, shows which plans churn drives from, and lists the at-risk segments: revenue with a scheduled cancellation, subscriptions on hold and customers with invoices in dunning.

It attempts the voluntary vs involuntary (failed payment) split and says plainly when the data doesn't support it. Takeaways point to the right follow-up: plan-performance, failed-payment-triage and dunning-review, or retention outreach drafted for the merchant to send.
triggers: Churn, retention, cancellations, "why are customers leaving?".
January churn, or which customers are at risk of cancelling.
examples: "How bad was churn this quarter?"
Ended subscriptions and MRR per month with the trend
"Who's at risk of cancelling?"
Scheduled cancellations, on-hold subscriptions and customers in dunning
"How much churn is from failed payments?"
The involuntary share if the data supports it, otherwise a clear 'not available'
notes: The voluntary vs involuntary split depends on `group_by=expire_reason` or a subscriptions export, both unconfirmed.
Not yet validated against live data.

migration-from-transform.summary: Guides Frisbii Transform customers moving to Frisbii Billing: migration plan, readiness check and a post-migration comparison of totals.
migration-from-transform.audience: Frisbii Transform customers moving to Frisbii Billing; Frisbii CS and migration team
migration-from-transform.week: Week 13 (18 Jan 2027), start of the Q1 migration mini-series
what: Asks where the merchant is in the move, then either walks through a seven-phase plan (inventory, concept mapping, payment-method token migration with Frisbii, catalogue build, test, cut-over, verify), runs a readiness check of the Billing catalogue (plans, add-ons, coupons, discounts, dunning plans), or compares the merchant's Transform totals with Frisbii Billing side by side.
The MCP only sees the Billing side, so Transform figures come from the merchant. The skill never creates anything and never asks for card data.
triggers: Migrating or moving from Frisbii Transform to Frisbii Billing.
A migration checklist, or checking that a migration is complete.
examples: "We're moving from Transform. Where do we start?"
A phased migration plan and a checklist with owners and dates
"Is our Billing catalogue ready?"
A readiness checklist of plans, add-ons, coupons, discounts and dunning plans
"Check our migration" (with Transform totals)
A Transform vs Billing comparison with differences above 1% flagged
notes: Draft migration content: must be reviewed by Frisbii's migration team before release.

Complements the [Frisbii Migration Toolkit](https://billwerk.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SKILL/pages/11604230630) (frisbii-com/frisbii-migration-toolkit), which re-codes the customer's own integration (API, checkout, portal, webhooks, cut-over). This skill covers migration planning and checking the migrated Billing data with the MCP; align the two before launch.
Not yet validated against live data.

dunning-review.summary: Reviews how well dunning recovers money: dunning plans, what is in dunning now, recovered vs lost, time to recover and where recovery stalls.
dunning-review.audience: Frisbii Pay and Billing merchants (finance, operations); Frisbii CS
what: Lists the dunning plans and retry schedules, shows invoices currently in dunning by step, and measures recovery over the last 90 days: invoices that settled after entering dunning (recovered) vs those that ended unpaid (lost), the recovery rate and the time to recover.
Suggestions are data-driven (e.g. late retries that add little, hard declines that retries can't fix, failed invoices outside any dunning flow) and are for the merchant to apply in the dashboard.
triggers: How dunning performs, recovery rate, "are my retries working?".
How long failed payments take to recover, or whether to change dunning settings.
examples: "How well do my retries work?"
Recovery rate, recovered vs lost amounts and the time-to-recover profile
"Where are invoices stuck in dunning?"
Invoices and amounts per dunning step with days overdue
"Should we change our dunning plan?"
Suggestions based on when recoveries actually happen
notes: Recovery is measured from settled invoices that carry a dunning timestamp via paged lists, so large accounts get a disclosed sample.
That timestamp field must be confirmed on live data.
Not yet validated against live data.

plan-performance.summary: Compares subscription plans: MRR, live subscriptions, growth, churn, revenue scheduled to cancel and coupon use per plan.
what: Builds a per-plan table from snapshot calls: live subscriptions, MRR and share, MRR per subscription, new and ended subscriptions over 90 days, an estimated churn ratio and the share of revenue already scheduled to cancel. Legacy (superseded) plans still billing are flagged.
Plan names come from `list_plans`, but the figures don't depend on it, so a `list_plans` failure only means plan handles are shown instead of names.
triggers: Which plans perform best, plan growth or churn.
"Which plan should we push or retire?", revenue by plan, a pricing review.
examples: "Which plans perform best?"
A per-plan table with MRR, growth, churn and at-risk share, plus highlights
"Which plan should we retire?"
Small, high-churn and legacy plans with the data behind the suggestion
"Which plans get discounted most?"
Coupon eligibility per plan, with an export offered for exact numbers
notes: Discounts per plan are only available via coupon eligibility or the subscription_discounts export.
Not yet validated against live data.
